subject: Demo performance acceptance criteria and MAP — action items & next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@fintechx.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Demo performance acceptance criteria and MAP — action items & next steps

Hi Asha / FinTechX team,

Thanks again for the time earlier — great to walk through the streaming demo and the high‑level integration path. Per our call, I pulled together the proposed performance acceptance criteria and a short mutual action plan so we can align on what success looks like for a pilot.

Performance acceptance criteria (proposed) — please confirm which items you want firmed up for the PoC:
- Latency: p95 generation latency (end-to-end request → first token) < 350 ms for batched non-streaming calls; for streaming flows, server chunk-to-client latency (per chunk) < 50 ms and p95 time-to-first-token < 200 ms.
- Throughput: sustained 500 requests/sec aggregate for model X (avg payload ~ 120 tokens/request) with occasional bursts to 900 rps for short windows (≤ 2 minutes).
- Concurrency: support 50 concurrent streams per model instance, with autoscaling policy to maintain latency SLOs.
- Streaming requirements: support chunked streaming with backpressure (max chunk size 256 tokens), ordered delivery, and max inter-chunk gap < 100 ms.
- Availability target for pilot: 99.5% uptime; SRE runbook handoff and monitoring dashboards available.
- Failover: automatic fallback to quantized variant within 500 ms if primary model degraded.

Notes on measurement: we will provide a standardized load test harness (script + sample payloads) and recommended tracing tags so both teams measure from the same telemetry. We'll also share the SLO matrix and perf profiles attached.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — owners & rough dates
- Redwood: provide SLO matrix + perf baseline (attachment: redwood_slo_matrix.xlsx) — owner: Marcus — due: 2026-07-26
- FinTechX: share representative prompt set and peak traffic windows (CSV + example traces) — owner: Asha — due: 2026-07-27
- Redwood: supply load-test harness + instructions, and run an initial baseline against hosted environment — owner: Dev Patel (cc’d internally) — due: 2026-07-30
- Joint: schedule capacity planning call to decide Dedicated vs Hosted pilot topology — owner: Neha — target week of 2026-08-02
- FinTechX: confirm security & encryption requirements for pilot (KMS/HSM scope) — owner: FinTechX security — due: 2026-07-30

Decision criteria we suggested during the demo (to confirm):
- If p95 latency consistently below thresholds on Hosted with acceptable cost, proceed with Hosted pilot + fallback Dedicated slice.
- If latency or throughput can't be met within cost targets, spin up a short Dedicated pilot (2 weeks) with reserved capacity sizing.

Attachments: redwood_slo_matrix.xlsx, perf-profiles.pdf (high-level traces and kernel selection notes).

Next steps: Asha, can you confirm which acceptance criteria are mandatory vs nice-to-have? Also confirm who from your procurement/security teams I should loop in for the pilot paperwork. After that we’ll lock dates for the capacity planning call.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin

From: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@fintechx.com>

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Demo performance acceptance criteria and MAP — action items & next steps

Marcus — thanks for the clear summary and for the attachments. Useful starting point. A few clarifying questions from our side before we sign off on the MAP: 

1) Streaming chunking: the demo used 128-token chunks — is the 256-token max chunk size you listed an upper bound or a recommendation? Our UX team prefers smaller chunk sizes (<= 128) to improve perceived latency on mobile. Will that change the server-side p95 numbers significantly?

2) For throughput: our avg payload will likely be closer to 80–100 tokens per request during peak. Can you share baseline tests for both 120-token and 80-token payloads so we can compare?

3) Concurrency semantics: is the 50 concurrent streams per model instance a per-customer cap or global per-instance cap? We need per-tenant isolation guarantees for multi-tenant hosted scenarios.

4) Security: for pilot data we require encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys (KMS). Does that require Dedicated, or can Hosted with customer KMS meet our compliance needs?

5) Quantization fallback: what is the expected latency uplift when falling back to the quantized variant? Our budget will tolerate up to 20% increase in p95 during fallback, but we want to avoid > 40% degradation.

We’ve attached a short internal doc with our expected peak windows and a sample trace (platform_peak_windows.xlsx). Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow morning to walk through these if easier.

Best,
Asha Reddy
Head of Platform — FinTechX
asha.reddy@fintechx.com
+1 202-555-0184

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 18:32:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Demo performance acceptance criteria and MAP — action items & next steps

Thanks Asha — good questions. Answering inline and proposing a practical pilot configuration: 

On Wed, Jul 22, 2026 at 4:05 PM Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@fintechx.com> wrote:
> 1) Streaming chunking: the demo used 128-token chunks — is the 256-token max chunk size you listed an upper bound or a recommendation?

256 is an upper bound and a conservative default for throughput tuning; 128-token chunks are fine and will typically improve perceived latency (smaller first-chunk serialization and quicker render on client). We should validate both in the load tests; we’ll include 80/120/128 test payloads.

> 2) For throughput: our avg payload will likely be closer to 80–100 tokens per request during peak. Can you share baseline tests for both 120-token and 80-token payloads so we can compare?

Yes — Marcus and I will run two baseline configurations and attach results. Expect the hosted baseline numbers by 2026-07-26 (per MAP item).

> 3) Concurrency semantics: is the 50 concurrent streams per model instance a per-customer cap or global per-instance cap?

That was meant as a per-instance concurrency target. For hosted multi-tenant setups we can provide per-tenant isolation controls (soft limits + throttles) and capacity reservations. If strict tenant isolation is required, Dedicated is the stronger option.

> 4) Security: for pilot data we require encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys (KMS). Does that require Dedicated, or can Hosted with customer KMS meet our compliance needs?

Hosted: we support customer-managed KMS for key wrapping (bring-your-own-key) for hosted customers in our enterprise tier — that does not require Dedicated, but there are additional onboarding steps. Dedicated: gives you more network isolation and full control over HSM integrations if needed. We’ll put a short decision matrix in the pilot proposal.

> 5) Quantization fallback: what is the expected latency uplift when falling back to the quantized variant?

Typical uplift depends on model and sequence length. For the family we demoed, moving to the 8-bit quantized variant we expect 10–25% p95 increase on average; we will report observed numbers from the baseline test. We will set an automatic rollback trigger if p95 > 1.4x baseline.

Proposed pilot (practical):
- 2-week Hosted pilot using reserved burst capacity with per-tenant reservations + Hosted KMS (if you want BYOK) — goal: validate p95 & throughput with your payloads.
- If Hosted pilot fails to meet mandatory acceptance criteria, spin up a 2-week Dedicated slice sized per baseline results.

Actions assigned now:
- Marcus: run baseline tests for 80/120 tokens and share results + traces — due 2026-07-26
- FinTechX (Asha): share final prompt set and procurement contact — due 2026-07-27
- Neha: circulate pilot-proposal.pdf (high-level topology + decision matrix) and schedule capacity call for week of 2026-08-02 — due 2026-07-24

Attachments: pilot-proposal.pdf (small), load-test harness repo link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-pilot-materials

I’ll kick off the calendar invite for the capacity planning call; Marcus will follow up with baseline artifacts.

Thanks — Neha
